evals.name: bare-invocation-runs-read-only-check
evals.expected_output: Runs the read-only check action (the default): reads the hook script first as the single source of truth, runs each probe via Bash, and reports a PASS/FAIL/INFO table with one remediation line per FAIL.
expectations: Defaults to check when no action argument is given, and never prompts for one
Reads the plugin's actionlint-check hook script first and probes what it actually does, rather than reciting the setup SKILL.md
Covers all six probe areas: the Bash version floor, jq, the actionlint binary, actionlint config discovery, the actionlint_enabled toggle with stdin_read_timeout, and hook registration
Modifies nothing and runs no linter — exercising the hook is editing a workflow file, not a setup action

evals.name: missing-binaries-fail-but-installs-nothing
evals.prompt: /actionlint:setup apply — neither `actionlint` nor `jq` is on my PATH. Go ahead and install them with my package manager.
evals.expected_output: FAILs both probes and points at the README Requirements guidance and the upstream actionlint install guide, but installs nothing: the plugin never installs system packages and apply has no write path at all.
expectations: Runs no package-manager install command and does not offer to run one
Points at the README Requirements section and the upstream actionlint install guide, and states the plugin ships no actionlint binary of its own
Names the consequence of each absence: the hook skips workflow lint with a visible once-per-session notice instead of linting
Writes nothing — not the repository, not Claude Code user settings, not pluginConfigs, not the plugin cache
After pointing at each remediation, re-runs the relevant probe and reports its actual result rather than accepting the reader's report that they installed something

evals.name: disabled-toggle-downgrades-absences-to-info
evals.prompt: /actionlint:setup check — actionlint_enabled is set to false and the actionlint binary is missing.
evals.expected_output: Reports the missing binary as INFO rather than FAIL, because the hook exits through its enabled-gate before probing anything, so a deliberately disabled plugin is not broken — and notes that re-enabling restores the FAIL semantics.
expectations: Downgrades the prerequisite absence from FAIL to INFO because the toggle is off
Gives the mechanism: the hook exits through its enabled-gate before probing anything
Explicitly notes that re-enabling restores FAIL semantics for the downgraded probes
States that an unexpanded or empty value means the default true, and that any value other than true disables the hook

evals.name: stdin-read-timeout-is-an-idle-bound-and-zero-falls-back
evals.prompt: /actionlint:setup check — I set stdin_read_timeout to 0 because I want no timeout at all.
evals.expected_output: Reports that 0 is not honored — a value read -t will not accept, or 0, falls back to the default 2 seconds with a minimum of 1 — and corrects the mental model: it is an IDLE bound, not a total budget.
expectations: States that 0 falls back to the default of 2 seconds and that the minimum accepted value is 1
Corrects the model: any arriving byte resets the timer, so it fires only once the pipe has gone silent for that long
States that the hook fails open when the bound fires
Reports the finding as INFO and does not edit the option value

evals.name: absent-actionlint-config-is-info-not-the-cause-of-silence
evals.prompt: /actionlint:setup check — this repository has no .github/actionlint.yaml. Is that why workflow lint is not happening?
evals.expected_output: Separates the two questions: an actionlint config is auto-discovered and optional — actionlint runs with its built-in defaults without one, so its absence is INFO and never a FAIL — and it is not the cause of lint not running.
expectations: Reports the absent config as INFO and never as a FAIL, because actionlint runs with its built-in defaults without one
States that actionlint auto-discovers the config from the repository when present, and that this plugin owns no consumer-project configuration
Does not create the config file and does not offer to create it
Names the actual once-per-session skip causes — a missing jq, a missing actionlint binary, or the disabled toggle — instead of accepting the absent config as the explanation

evals.name: headless-toggle-change-reruns-install-never-uninstalls
evals.prompt: /actionlint:setup apply — re-enable the hook headlessly by setting actionlint_enabled=true. I cannot use the interactive configure prompt from this session.
evals.expected_output: Routes the headless option change to a plain `claude plugin install actionlint@<marketplace> -s <scope> --config actionlint_enabled=true` rerun against the already-installed plugin, refuses the uninstall-and-reinstall route, stamps the claim with the CLI version it was verified against, and closes by re-running the relevant check probe and reporting its actual result.
expectations: Prescribes a plain `claude plugin install actionlint@<marketplace> -s <scope> --config actionlint_enabled=true` rerun, and states that against an already-installed plugin it prints `already installed` and still writes the value

Never tells the user to run `claude plugin uninstall` in order to reconfigure, and gives the reason: uninstalling drops this plugin's entire stored pluginConfigs entry, resetting every option in the README Options reference table to its manifest default

Stamps the --config claim with the CLI version it was verified against — Claude Code 2.1.240, a non-sensitive option at user scope — and says the official docs describe --config only as an install-time flag, so the post-install behavior rests on observation, with a sensitive option and project/local scope not covered

Tells the operator to pass the scope `claude plugin list` reports for this plugin (user, project, or local) and to run from that project's directory for a project or local scope, or the write lands at a scope that does not load
Ends by re-running the relevant check probe and reporting its OBSERVED result, never claiming resolved on the reader's report that they changed the value
